purpose: Define an advisory proof request fingerprint and verdict receipt contract so repeated validation requests can be compared, reused, or refused without claiming bead completion by receipt alone.

proof_request_fingerprint.id_algorithm: sha256 over canonical proof_request JSON after the canonicalization rules below

canonicalization.json_encoding: utf8 JSON with sorted object keys and no insignificant whitespace
canonicalization.argv_normalization: preserve command argv order exactly after path separators and repeated whitespace inside each argument are normalized
canonicalization.env_normalization: keep only accepted env allowlist entries, sort by name, and redact values not marked fingerprint-safe
canonicalization.path_normalization: store repository-relative paths with forward slashes; reject absolute target-dir and temp paths unless their policy name is included
canonicalization.set_normalization: sort feature flags, dirty paths, dependency closure roots, source evidence ids, and allowed env names lexicographically

required_inputs.reason: The command shape is the primary proof surface and argv order is semantic.
Cargo check, Cargo test, clippy, shell, jq, and docs-only proof requests are not interchangeable.
Only declared environment variables can influence the fingerprint.
Package-scoped Rust proof cannot satisfy a different package.
Library tests, integration tests, all-targets checks, and shell gates have different coverage.
Specific integration tests and lib-test filters must remain distinguishable.
A filtered proof cannot be widened or narrowed silently.
Feature selection changes compiled code and test reachability.
Receipts are anchored to a specific commit or source revision.
Clean, dirty, and mixed worktrees are separate proof states.
Dirty-file overlap can invalidate otherwise matching receipts.
Changes under these roots invalidate cached proof even when the command text is unchanged.
RCH behavior and local-fallback detection are part of proof trust.
remote, local-fallback, direct-local, and shell-only proof requests have different trust levels.
Shared, disposable, warmed, and unknown target-dir policies affect contamination risk.
Closeout, regression, smoke, docs, and exploratory proofs have different reuse authority.
Agent ownership makes duplicate-proof and collision diagnosis auditable.
A request without br, Agent Mail, git, or RCH evidence cannot support reuse.

rejected_shapes: shell-wrapped rch command that can fail open into local cargo
rch transcript with local fallback markers
proof command missing CARGO_TARGET_DIR policy for Rust validation
all-targets proof claimed as an exact filtered proof

statuses.meaning: The proof command completed successfully and all required artifacts are complete.
The proof command ran but did not pass. It can explain failure, not satisfy green proof.
The receipt no longer matches current source, dependency, toolchain, RCH, or TTL state.
The proof surface observed local fallback, dirty overlap, or other contamination.
The broker lacks enough evidence to decide reuse.
The broker has enough evidence to reject reuse for this request.

reuse_policy: Only passed receipts may be reused, and only when the proof request fingerprint is exact or later equivalence logic proves the request stronger without changing the accepted inputs.
Failed receipts may be reused as failure evidence only; they cannot satisfy closeout or green proof.
Stale, contaminated, inconclusive, and reuse_refused receipts cannot satisfy acceptance or close a bead.
A verdict receipt is evidence only. It cannot mutate br state, release reservations, send Agent Mail, or mark a bead closed by itself.

invalidation_reasons.description: The validation command returned a failing exit status.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Inspect the captured artifact bundle, fix the failing behavior or environment issue, and rerun the exact proof request.

invalidation_reasons.description: A source path in the request or dependency closure changed after the receipt was emitted.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Rerun the proof from the current source revision and record the new git commit and dirty-path summary.

invalidation_reasons.description: A dependency closure root changed, including sibling crates or script fixtures that influence the request.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Refresh dependency closure evidence and rerun a proof that covers the changed root.

invalidation_reasons.description: The RCH client, daemon, or remote-worker posture changed since the receipt.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Capture the new RCH version/posture and rerun the exact command through the current RCH path.

invalidation_reasons.description: Rust toolchain, Cargo metadata, or relevant shell tool versions changed.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Record the current toolchain metadata and rerun the proof request against that toolchain.

invalidation_reasons.description: The transcript contains RCH local fallback or direct local execution markers for a proof that required remote execution.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Do not reuse the receipt. Rerun with a remote-only RCH path or downgrade to a shell/json proof if the lane is non-Rust.

invalidation_reasons.description: The current dirty paths differ from the receipt or overlap the proof surface unexpectedly.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Refresh the dirty-path summary, isolate unrelated edits, and rerun the proof with the current overlap recorded.

invalidation_reasons.description: The receipt exceeded its freshness deadline.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Rerun the proof request or extend reuse only after a fresh broker receipt proves the same fingerprint remains valid.

invalidation_reasons.description: Required artifacts such as run_manifest.json, events.jsonl, commands.txt, transcript, or report are missing or unreadable.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Regenerate the full artifact bundle and rerun smoke validation before considering reuse.

invalidation_reasons.description: The cached receipt proves a narrower surface than the requested command.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Run the requested wider command or file a separate bead that explicitly accepts the narrower proof.

invalidation_reasons.description: The cached receipt is broader than the requested surface and current-head drift could hide target-specific behavior.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Rerun the exact requested filtered proof or attach equivalence evidence in the later classifier lane.

invalidation_reasons.description: The request or receipt lacks required br, Agent Mail, git, RCH, or artifact evidence.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Capture the missing evidence source and emit a new receipt before any reuse decision.

invalidation_reasons.description: The command shape cannot be classified safely, such as shell-wrapped cargo or an unrecognized local build wrapper.
invalidation_reasons.required_remediation: Normalize the command into an accepted RCH, bash syntax, jq, or git diff proof shape and rerun.
